paper.title: Conformal Sequential Decision Making With Cost and Sublinear Policy Regret Guarantees

settings.name_in_paper: Episodic sequential decision problem with per-episode cost constraints and policy regret
unmapped: Horizon partitioned into J episodes of lengths n_1..n_J; reward and cost depend on action, exogenous arbitrary state, and within-episode history (memory reset each episode)
Per-episode average cost must be <= budget level D (D is a cost budget, not a delay) deterministically; a zero-cost action A* exists
Learner observes only the block reward of the chosen nominal action (bandit feedback per episode)
Learner knows J, n_max, r_min, Delta_r and the cost budget D
Comparator class: constant nominal action with the same cost-enforcing switch to the zero-cost action, evaluated along its own history
settings.definition_quote: We consider a sequential decision problem over a time horizon~$T$ that is partitioned into $J$ consecutive blocks, or episodes. ... reward $r_{j,k}=r(A_{j,k},X_{j,k},H_{j,k})\in[r\sub{min},r\sub{max}]$ ... cost $c_{j,k}=c(A_{j,k},X_{j,k},H_{j,k})\in[0,1]$ ... $\Pr[\max_{j\in[J]} C_j(A_{1:T})\le D]=1$ for every state sequence

algorithms.name: OCEA (online conformal episodic agent; blockwise EXP3 with cost-enforcing switch)

conditions: n_max, K, Delta r fixed and independent of T
history (memory) reset at the beginning of each episode

source.label: thm:blockwise-exp3
source.quote: Under the zero-cost assumption \eqref{eq:safe-action}, the actions generated by the OCEA policy satisfy the constraint \eqref{eq:reliability-objective} for every realization of the learner's randomization. Moreover, let $\gamma = \min\{1, \sqrt{K\ln K/((e-1)J)}\}$. The expected policy regret satisfies $\max_{i\in[K]} \sum_{j=1}^{J}R_j(i) - \mathbb E [ \sum_{j=1}^{J}R_j(I_j) ] \le 2.63 \Delta r n_{\max}\sqrt{KT\ln K}$

results.notes: Also guarantees per-episode cost constraint deterministically. Proof uses J <= T; tuning requires knowledge of J. Environment mapped to bounded-memory adversary since rewards depend on within-episode history.

cited_results.setting_description: Adversarial K-armed bandit with rewards in [0,1], J rounds
Bandit policy regret against adaptive adversaries with unbounded memory
